body:
maria: Heads-up — drafting a proposal for handling high-cardinality span attributes from prompts and request metadata. Need opinions on where to hash/scrub (collector vs ingestion), bucket sizing, and Console UX impact.

kevin: Agreed. Two hard constraints: keep Console metrics useful per-route (latency/cost) and avoid exploding label cardinality in Prometheus/Kafka. Also want stable groups for debugging while preserving privacy.

samir: For prompt text: HMAC-SHA256 fingerprinting with a rotating salt + keep a small top-k fingerprint list per-project for evals. Never persist raw prompt in telemetry.

julia: If we rotate salts we should annotate span attrs with salt_version (e.g., prompt_fp_v3) so offline re-hashes are possible for incident investigations. Don’t keep raw prompt anywhere.

kevin: Scrub point options: exporter-side (collector) rewrite — pros: saves bandwidth/storage early; cons: harder to reprocess later. Ingest-side — pros: reprocessable; cons: raw data custody and storage cost.

maria: Leaning hybrid: collector performs default minimization (drop known PII keys, HMAC prompt), ingestion keeps an encrypted debug blob for short TTL (7d) for on-call debugging (audited access), then truncate.

samir: For request_id and user_id use bucketization (hash mod N) rather than raw hashes: choose N per-tenant (dev small, prod large). This lets us bound label cardinality and sample by bucket.

kevin: Also propose a Bloom filter at ingest for heavy hitters to allow cheap membership tests without storing the raw id. Tag spans with bucket_id for dashboards.

julia: Console effects: top-request-id lists should show bucket_id view + "bucket sample" counts. Provide clear help text explaining privacy-preserving bucketing and an ops audit link for 7d access.

maria: Retention and quotas proposal: 7d encrypted debug blob (tight ACL), 90d bucketed/hashed spans, 365d aggregated metrics. If any attr exceeds cardinality threshold, auto-sample and emit an alert.

kevin: Auto-sampling: when a label's cardinality > threshold, compute sample_rate = clamp(0.01, 1, target_cardinality/observed_cardinality) and apply probabilistic sampling by bucket. Emit tag sampling_reason and sample_rate on spans.

samir: For prompt fingerprints keep a short-lived cache (redis) of recent fingerprints per-project (e.g., 10k TTL 24h) for deduping and eval alignment. Only fingerprints, never raw prompts.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: scrub-policy-v2 -> collector config Tue 03:00 UTC. Rolling 50% -> 100% in 1h if no errors.

julia: Rollout UX idea: in Console rollout page show scrub-policy diff preview: which attributes will be removed or rewritten, estimated cardinality reduction, and a rollback button that reverts collector config and re-enables debug blob for 1h.

maria: Open questions: salt rotation cadence? monthly? N bucket defaults per tier (dev=32, staging=128, prod=1024)? Legal ok with 7d encrypted debug blob?

kevin: Monthly rotation seems fine. Make bucket counts configurable per-tenant. I'll loop in compliance on the 7d blob.

samir: Action items:
- maria: author collector scrub config + sample grep rules (EOD Wed)
- kevin: PR for bucketization + Bloom filter design
- julia: Console mockups + help copy
- legal: compliance review (maria to ping)

maria: Example collector snippet for discussion:

processors:
  prompt_sanitizer:
    match_keys: ["http.request.prompt", "llm.prompt"]
    hash_hmac: true
    salt_version: "v1"
    keep_example_fp: true

exporters:
  redwood_ingest:
    send_debug_blob: true
    debug_blob_ttl_days: 7

kevin: Also add a linter in service templates that flags new span attrs with many unique values in dev. Normalize metric labels to prevent freeform labels.

julia: I'll add a Console banner for "high-cardinality label detected" linking to the scrub policy docs.

maria: Great. We'll reconvene after the config PRs land. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
